questions.question: Who called the preamble of the Indian Constitution ‘The Political Horoscope of our Constitution’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. KM Munshi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. KM Munshi** referred to the preamble of the Indian Constitution as 'The Political Horoscope of our Constitution'.
 
• The preamble serves as an introduction to the Constitution and outlines the guiding principles and philosophy of the document.
 
• It reflects the aspirations and values of the people of India, including justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
 
• The preamble plays a crucial role in interpreting the Constitution and understanding the intent of its framers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The preamble is considered an integral part of the Constitution and has been referred to in various landmark judgments by the Supreme Court of India.
 
• Dr. KM Munshi was a prominent member of the Constituent Assembly and played a significant role in drafting the Constitution.
 
• The preamble has been amended once by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, which added the words 'socialist', 'secular', and 'integrity'.

questions.question: At which place is Harappan Dockyard found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lothal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Harappan Dockyard is found at **Lothal**, one of the prominent sites of the Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• Lothal is located in the present-day state of **Gujarat, India**.
 
• The dockyard at Lothal is considered one of the world's earliest known docks and was crucial for maritime trade in ancient times.
 
• This dockyard connected the city to an ancient course of the Sabarmati river, which was crucial for trade and commerce.
 
• The discovery of the dockyard has provided significant insights into the engineering and maritime skills of the Harappan people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indus Valley Civilization, also known as the Harappan Civilization, was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations.
 
• It flourished in the basins of the Indus River, which flows through present-day Pakistan, and along the Ghaggar-Hakra River, which once flowed through northwest India and eastern Pakistan.
 
• Other major Harappan sites include **Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Dholavira, and Rakhigarhi**.
 
• The civilization is noted for its advanced urban planning, architecture, and social organization.
 
• Artifacts such as seals, pottery, and jewelry found at Harappan sites provide valuable insights into the culture and daily life of the people.

questions.question: Which is the weakest intermolecular force, considered as the Van der Waals force, often found in halogens, noble gases and other non-polar molecules?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**London dispersion forces**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **London dispersion forces** are the weakest intermolecular forces.
 
• These forces are a type of **Van der Waals force** and are present in all atoms and molecules, but are most significant in non-polar molecules.
 
• They arise due to temporary fluctuations in electron density, which create instantaneous dipoles.

questions.question: Which chromosome is involved in the production of ‘masked’ mRNAs for early development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lampbrush chromosome**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lampbrush chromosomes** are involved in the production of 'masked' mRNAs for early development.
 
• These chromosomes are a special form of chromosome found in the growing oocytes (immature egg cells) of most animals, except mammals.
 
• The lampbrush chromosomes are characterized by their large size and distinctive appearance, which is due to the extensive looping of chromatin.
 
• They play a crucial role in gene transcription during early development, producing mRNAs that are stored and later used during embryogenesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Masked mRNAs** are mRNA molecules that are transcribed but not immediately translated into proteins; they are stored in the cytoplasm and translated at a later stage.
 
• The structure of lampbrush chromosomes allows for high levels of transcriptional activity, which is necessary for the rapid cell divisions and developmental processes in early embryogenesis.
 
• Lampbrush chromosomes were first observed by Walther Flemming in 1882, and their detailed structure was later described by Ruckert in 1892.
 
• The study of lampbrush chromosomes has provided significant insights into the organization and function of chromatin and the regulation of gene expression.

questions.question: The festival of Ram Navami is celebrated in which of the following Hindu months?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaitra**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ram Navami** is celebrated in the Hindu month of **Chaitra**.
 
• It marks the birth of **Lord Rama**, the seventh avatar of the deity Vishnu.
 
• The festival typically falls in the Gregorian months of **March or April**.
 
• Devotees celebrate the day with fasting, reading the **Ramayana**, and participating in **processions and prayers**.
 
• The day is considered highly auspicious and is observed with great devotion across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Rama** is considered a symbol of **virtue and righteousness**.
 
• The epic **Ramayana**, which narrates the life of Lord Rama, is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient Indian literature, the other being the **Mahabharata**.
 
• The celebrations of Ram Navami also include **recitals of devotional hymns and kirtans** in praise of Lord Rama.
 
• In some regions, **Ratha Yatra** (chariot procession) is organized, where the idols of Lord Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, and Hanuman are taken out in a grand procession.
 
• The festival underscores the importance of adherence to **truth, morality, and duty** as exemplified by Lord Rama's life.

questions.question: Which of the following movement is known as first Satyagraha led by Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Champaran movement**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Champaran movement** was the first Satyagraha led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1917.
 
• It was initiated to address the grievances of farmers in the Champaran district of Bihar who were forced to grow indigo under oppressive conditions by British planters.
 
• This movement marked Gandhi's first active involvement in Indian freedom struggle and showcased his method of non-violent resistance.
 
• The success of the Champaran movement established Gandhi as a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** employed the strategy of Satyagraha, which is a form of non-violent resistance or civil resistance.
 
• The **Kheda movement** followed the Champaran movement in 1918, focusing on relief for farmers in Gujarat affected by crop failure and plague.
 
• The **Ahmedabad movement** in 1918 was another significant Satyagraha where Gandhi supported mill workers demanding better wages.
 
• The **Quit India Movement** launched in 1942 was a mass protest demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• These movements collectively contributed to the mobilization of the Indian populace against British rule and were pivotal in India's journey to independence.

questions.question: The Constitution of India was adopted on 26th November in _________.

__
 
• The Constitution of India was adopted on **26th November 1949**.
 
• It was drafted by the Constituent Assembly, which was formed in 1946.
 
• The drafting committee was chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, who is often referred to as the principal architect of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Constitution came into effect on **26th January 1950**, which is celebrated as Republic Day in India.
 
• The adoption of the Constitution marked the transition of India from a British Dominion to a fully sovereign republic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written constitution** of any country in the world.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The Constitution has undergone several amendments since its adoption to address emerging issues and changing needs of the country.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.

questions.question: In which state is the Sambhar Salt Lake located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Sambhar Salt Lake is located in the state of **Rajasthan**, India.
 
• It is India's largest inland salt lake and is situated about 80 km southwest of the city of Jaipur.
 
• The lake is an important source of salt production and is also a designated Ramsar site, recognizing its importance as a wetland ecosystem.
 
• The Sambhar Salt Lake is fed by several freshwater streams, including the Mendha, Rupangarh, Khandel, and Kharian rivers.
 
• The lake's surroundings are rich in biodiversity, supporting various bird species, including flamingos, pelicans, and storks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajasthan** is the largest state in India by area and is known for its rich cultural heritage and historical significance.
 
• The state is home to several UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including the Hill Forts of Rajasthan and the Keoladeo National Park.
 
• Rajasthan's economy is primarily based on agriculture, mining, and tourism, with significant contributions from the salt industry.
 
• The state experiences an arid to semi-arid climate, with hot summers and mild winters, making it suitable for salt production.
 
• Rajasthan is also famous for its palaces, forts, and vibrant festivals, attracting tourists from around the world.
 
• The state capital, Jaipur, is part of the Golden Triangle tourist circuit, along with Delhi and Agra.

questions.question: Which neighbouring country has assumed the chairmanship of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) from November 2021 to November 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangladesh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bangladesh** assumed the chairmanship of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) from November 2021 to November 2023.
 
• The IORA is an inter-governmental organization aimed at strengthening regional cooperation and sustainable development within the Indian Ocean region.
 
• Bangladesh's chairmanship focuses on enhancing maritime safety and security, trade and investment facilitation, fisheries management, disaster risk management, and tourism and cultural exchanges among member states.
 
• IORA's chairmanship rotates every two years among member countries to ensure diverse leadership and representation.
 
• Bangladesh's leadership in IORA is seen as a significant opportunity to bolster regional cooperation and economic growth within the Indian Ocean region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) was established in 1997 and comprises 23 member states bordering the Indian Ocean.
 
• IORA's primary objective is to promote sustainable development and balanced growth in the region through economic cooperation.
 
• The Association also includes dialogue partners such as China, the United States, and the United Kingdom, who collaborate on various initiatives.
 
• Bangladesh's chairmanship coincides with its growing role in regional and international forums, highlighting its commitment to multilateral cooperation.
 
• Key areas of cooperation under IORA include maritime safety and security, trade and investment, fisheries management, disaster risk management, academic and scientific cooperation, and tourism and cultural exchanges.

questions.question: As of December 2021, NPS and APY are the two flagship pension schemes of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PFRDA**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PFRDA** stands for the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority.
 
• As of December 2021, the **National Pension System (NPS)** and the **Atal Pension Yojana (APY)** are the two flagship pension schemes regulated by the PFRDA.
 
• The **NPS** is a voluntary, defined contribution retirement savings scheme designed to enable subscribers to make optimum decisions regarding their future through systematic savings during their working life.
 
• **APY** is a government-backed pension scheme targeted primarily at the unorganized sector, aiming to provide a universal social security system for all Indians, especially the poor, the underprivileged, and the workers in the unorganized sector.
 
• The PFRDA was established by the Government of India in 2003 and it regulates and develops the pension sector in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **National Pension System (NPS)** was launched on 1st January 2004 with the objective of providing retirement income to all the citizens.
 
• **Atal Pension Yojana (APY)** was launched on 9th May 2015 and aims to deliver old age income security particularly to the workers in the unorganized sector.
 
• The PFRDA ensures the orderly growth and development of the pension market in India.
 
• Both NPS and APY are aimed at encouraging the habit of saving for retirement among the citizens.

questions.question: In which of the following sports/games is the term 'checkmate' used?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chess**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **'checkmate'** is used in the game of **Chess**.
 
• Checkmate is a position in chess in which a player's king is in a position to be captured (in check) and there is no way to move the king out of capture (mate).
 
• Achieving checkmate is the primary objective in a game of chess, resulting in a win for the player who checkmates their opponent.
 
• Chess is a two-player strategy board game that has been played for centuries and is known for its deep strategic elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chess originated in India around the 6th century AD and has evolved over the centuries into the modern game we know today.
 
• The game is played on an 8x8 grid called a chessboard, and each player starts with 16 pieces: one king, one queen, two rooks, two knights, two bishops, and eight pawns.
 
• Chess is recognized as a sport by the International Olympic Committee, and the World Chess Federation (FIDE) oversees international chess competitions.
 
• The game promotes cognitive skills such as problem-solving, strategic thinking, and pattern recognition.

questions.question: Bhabru-Bairat rock edicts mainly depicting Ashokas' conversion to Buddhism is found in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhabru-Bairat rock edicts** are inscriptions attributed to Emperor Ashoka of the Maurya Dynasty.
 
• These edicts primarily depict Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism and his efforts to spread Buddhist teachings.
 
• The Bhabru-Bairat rock edicts are found in the state of **Rajasthan**, India.
 
• They are significant historical records that provide insights into Ashoka's reign and his dedication to Buddhism.
 
• The edicts are written in the Brahmi script and are among several other rock and pillar edicts scattered across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ashoka, also known as Ashoka the Great, was the third ruler of the Maurya Dynasty and is considered one of India's greatest emperors.
 
• He ruled from approximately 268 to 232 BCE and his reign marked a significant period in Indian history.
 
• Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism is believed to have been influenced by the aftermath of the Kalinga War, which resulted in massive loss of life and suffering.
 
• Following his conversion, Ashoka promoted the spread of Buddhism both within and outside his empire, sending missionaries to various regions.
 
• The rock edicts of Ashoka are a testament to his efforts to govern by moral principles and promote dharma (righteousness).

questions.question: Article 171 deals with ________.

options.text: qualifications of the Chief Minister of a State
qualifications of the Governor of a State

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**composition of the Legislative Councils**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 171** of the Indian Constitution deals with the **composition of the Legislative Councils**.
 
• The Legislative Council is the upper house in those states of India that have a bicameral legislature.
 
• According to Article 171, the total number of members in the Legislative Council of a state shall not exceed one-third of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that state.
 
• The members of the Legislative Council are elected by various groups including the Legislative Assembly, graduates, teachers, and local authority members.
 
• The Governor of the state also nominates some members to the Legislative Council.

• **Article 168** of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the Legislative Council in states.
